sourceNote: The copy beaver-edit.glb (armSource) with new quad tubes on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist, 1.5 times longer than the arms of the source. tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py --factor 1.5 makes these faces. The other faces stay as in beaver-edit.glb.
armSourceNote: A copy of beaver.glb with the arms free of the trunk (tools/blender/beaver_edit.py, assets/models/beaver/README.md). tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py reads it. beaver.glb stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the weight rules of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, as on the wolf.
name: Beaver

app.note: The size of the parametric beaver: the scale puts the standing skull top (the highest vertex within 0.03 u of the middle plane, 1.0 u) at 1.029 m. The reach goes from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 keeps the arm length, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms. The arms of beaver-arms.glb are 1.5 times longer than the arms of the source (arm_rebuild.py --factor 1.5), and the arm joints are the joints of the longer arms, so the reach stays app.reach. The beaver plays a smaller bassoon (SpeciesParams.bassoonScale, SPECIES_WIND_HOLDS.beaver of src/pose/winds.ts).

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py (step_skeleton() prints it).
armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube.

legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh, and the chair fits the legs. The seat of the legs of the seated bind is 0.072 m, and the chair of the app is 0.159 m deep.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The broad flat tail has two bones. The joints of the left arm beyond the shoulder are the joints of the turned arm of beaver-edit.glb, 1.5 times longer (tools/blender/beaver_edit.py --factor 1.5 prints them).

studio.bindArmsNote: With straightArms, bindArms.upper_arm sets the bind upper arm, and bindArms.forearm sets only the elbow axis: the cross product of the bind upper arm and this forearm direction (StudioBody.hinges, bind_hinges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The two directions are the directions of the old bent bind, so that the elbow axes and the zero of the roll of the upper arm stay. The paw has no bind direction, because it keeps the turn of the upper arm.
studio.straightArmsNote: The bind keeps the arms of the source straight: the forearm and the paw keep the turn of the upper arm, so that the rest shape holds the bend of no role, and each hold bends the elbow and the wrist from the same shape (the role-neutral bind of design 4.4).
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of each arm turns about its bind forearm toward supination, the left 124 degrees and the right 71 degrees (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The forearm segments share the turn. Each value makes the largest paw twist p95 of the six roles of the cast matrix and the bassoon smallest (design 4.4, pnpm bind-supination beaver): about 110 degrees on the left (the violin and the snare drum) and 72 degrees on the right (the cello), against 165 and 143 degrees with no supination. A second probe of the supinated rig moves the left side 4 degrees and the right side less than 1 degree.
studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). tailBind turns the two tail bones 10 and 25 degrees below the level, so that the tail end lies on the floor behind the chair.

tail.note: The tail has two bones: the vertices within radius of the line from the root over the bend to the tip, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The broad tail goes 0.124 u out to each side of the line.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, and the mouse.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, and the mouse.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the round haunch stays on the hips.

weights.rigidPaintedNote: The faces at these points take the mean of the painted weights of their corners, as rigid does for the rule weights. The first item holds two thin faces at the front of the left shoulder, and the second item eight thin faces in the front crease of the right arm root, where tools/blender/beaver_edit.py split the arm from the trunk. Each of these faces folded in each sample of the bassoon (pnpm fold-probe bassoonist). The last three items are single thin faces of the left paw, the right paw, and the right shoulder.
weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex follows the head only. The small ears join the head below the skull top, so earBase lies above the head and the ears follow the head.

flip.note: The values of the other meshes.

refine.ringsNote: The config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh beaver --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

check.note: The values of the other meshes.

colors.note: A dark face in the eye box is a face of an eye. A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color (the mean of the dark pad) than to white is a face of the nose and takes the gloss.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the hippo, and the mouse.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the skin normals with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). This removes the dark wedge under each raised arm.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x 0.23). The front edge lies behind the shins, and the back edge lies 0.01 u behind the root of the tail.

crease.note: The values of the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, and the mouse.

sit.note: The values of the panda, the hippo, and the mouse.
